usage: Exactly how it reads on a Korean clothing tag; say it '면 백 퍼센트'.
순(純)+면; common on bedding and baby clothes labels.
면 + item is the normal way to describe what something is made of.
소재 = material/fabric; staff use this word a lot when describing clothes.
examples: 이거 면이에요, 아니면 합성섬유예요?
Is this cotton, or is it synthetic?
The exact question to ask before buying clothes you'll wash a lot.
여름엔 면 소재가 시원해서 좋아요.
In summer cotton material is nice because it's cool.
시원하다 (already known) pairs naturally with breathable fabrics.
면 100%라서 세탁하면 좀 줄어들 수 있어요.
It's 100% cotton, so it may shrink a bit when you wash it.
줄어들다 (shrink) is the practical warning shop staff give about cotton.
nuance: 면 is the everyday word for cotton fabric, and you'll see it constantly on Korean clothing and bedding tags. Be careful: 면 spelled the same way also means 'noodles,' so context (clothes vs. food) is what tells them apart. For describing what an item is made of, Koreans just say 면 + the item, like 면 티셔츠.
mistakes: Confusing 면 (cotton) with 솜, which is the fluffy cotton stuffing/wool inside padding, not the woven fabric.
Saying 면으로 만든 것 every time — natural speech just uses 면 티셔츠, 면 바지 directly.

usage: What you ask for when you don't want fake; 진짜 (already known) = real.
Colloquial term; the formal label word is 인조가죽 (artificial leather).
소(cow)+가죽; the most common leather type for bags and shoes.
가죽 + item, the standard way to say a leather thing.
examples: 이 가방 진짜 가죽이에요?
Is this bag real leather?
The key question at a leather-goods shop or market.
가죽 제품은 비 오는 날 조심해야 해요.
You have to be careful with leather products on rainy days.
조심하다 (already known); practical care advice you'll hear.
진짜 가죽치고 가격이 너무 싼데요?
For real leather, the price is awfully cheap, isn't it?
N치고 = 'for/considering a N'; a natural way to express suspicion about a deal.
nuance: 가죽 covers all kinds of leather, and shops distinguish 진짜 가죽 (real) from 인조가죽 or 합성피혁 (synthetic) on tags. In casual speech people just say 가짜 가죽 for fake. Leather is a big category at Korean markets like Dongdaemun, so knowing how to ask 진짜 가죽이에요? saves you from overpaying.
mistakes: Using 피부 (skin, for humans/skincare) instead of 가죽 — 피부 is your skin, 가죽 is the material.
Assuming all 가죽 is real; vendors may call PU/synthetic leather 가죽 loosely, so confirm with 진짜?

usage: Reads on sweater and coat tags; pronounced '울 백 퍼센트'.
울 + item; the warm winter coat everyone buys for Korean winters.
양(sheep)+모(hair); the more technical word seen on care labels.
니트 (already known) + 울 to specify the material.
examples: 이 코트 울 몇 퍼센트예요?
What percentage wool is this coat?
A smart question, since blends are common and affect warmth and price.
울은 따뜻하지만 물세탁하면 안 돼요.
Wool is warm, but you can't machine-wash it.
따뜻하다 (already known); 물세탁 = washing with water, a real care tip.
울 스웨터는 드라이클리닝 맡기는 게 좋아요.
It's best to take wool sweaters to dry cleaning.
맡기다 (already known) = to entrust/drop off; the recommended care for wool.
nuance: 울 is the standard borrowed word for wool, used everywhere on Korean winter-clothing tags. The native/formal equivalent 양모 appears on care labels but people say 울 in conversation. Since Korean winters are cold, 울 코트 and 울 니트 are common purchases, and asking the wool percentage signals you know quality.
mistakes: Writing 월 (month) instead of 울 (wool) — they look similar but are completely different words.
Machine-washing 울 because you didn't read the label; real wool needs 드라이클리닝 or hand washing.

usage: 실크 + item; scarves are the most common silk purchase as gifts.
On the tag of nicer blouses and scarves.
같은 (like) makes it describe texture rather than actual material.
Native term seen with 한복 (hanbok) and traditional goods.
examples: 실크라서 손세탁만 가능해요.
Since it's silk, only hand-washing is possible.
손세탁 = hand washing; the standard care for delicate silk.
이 스카프 실크예요? 촉감이 정말 부드럽네요.
Is this scarf silk? The feel is really soft.
촉감 = touch/feel; 부드럽다 (already known) is the word for silk's texture.
선물용으로 실크 스카프 하나 살까 해요.
I'm thinking of buying a silk scarf as a gift.
V-(으)ㄹ까 하다 = 'thinking of doing'; 선물용 = for-gift purpose.
nuance: 실크 is the common loanword for silk and dominates everyday speech, while 비단 is the traditional word you'll meet around hanbok and traditional crafts. Silk items in Korea are usually scarves, blouses, and gift sets, and they're prized for being 부드럽다 (soft). Always check care labels, because real silk needs gentle hand washing.
mistakes: Using 비단 in a modern department store — staff understand it but everyone says 실크 there.
Expecting to machine-wash 실크; it almost always needs 손세탁 or dry cleaning.

usage: 용기 = container; the everyday word for tupperware-type items.
플라스틱 + item to say what it's made of.
쓰레기 (already known); relevant for Korea's strict recycling.
전자레인지 (already known) + 용 (for-use); important when buying containers.
examples: 이 용기 플라스틱이에요? 전자레인지에 돌려도 돼요?
Is this container plastic? Can I microwave it?
돌리다 (to run/spin) is the casual verb for 'microwave it.'
플라스틱은 분리수거 잘 해야 해요.
You have to sort plastic properly for recycling.
분리수거 (already known) is strictly enforced in Korean apartments.
저렴한 건 플라스틱이고 비싼 건 유리예요.
The cheap ones are plastic and the expensive ones are glass.
Contrasting materials by price, a common in-store comparison.
nuance: 플라스틱 is the all-purpose word for plastic, from containers to chairs to packaging. Because Korea enforces 분리수거 (waste sorting) strictly, knowing this word matters beyond just shopping. When buying food containers, asking whether the 플라스틱 is microwave-safe (전자레인지용) is a genuinely useful real-life question.
mistakes: Calling all containers 플라스틱 when many kitchen ones are 유리 (glass) or 스테인리스 (stainless) — check first.
Pronouncing it like English 'plastic'; in Korean it's 플라스틱 with clear separate syllables.

usage: 컵 (already known); the standard drinking glass.
Often marketed as healthier/heat-safe vs. plastic.
강화 = strengthened; common for phone screen protectors and cookware.
(으)로 된 = made of; a natural way to specify material.
examples: 유리 용기는 무겁지만 더 위생적이에요.
Glass containers are heavy but more hygienic.
무겁다 (already known); 위생적 = hygienic, a common selling point.
이 컵 유리예요? 깨질까 봐 걱정돼요.
Is this cup glass? I'm worried it might break.
깨지다 (already known) + V-(으)ㄹ까 봐 = worry that it might break.
휴대폰에 강화유리 하나 붙이려고요.
I'm planning to put a tempered glass on my phone.
붙이다 = to stick on; 강화유리 is what you ask for at a phone-accessory shop.
nuance: 유리 means glass as a material and shows up for cups, containers, and 강화유리 (tempered glass) screen protectors. Shoppers often weigh 유리 against 플라스틱: glass is heavier and breakable but seen as cleaner and microwave/oven-safe. Note 유리 is also a common woman's given name, so context tells you which is meant.
mistakes: Mixing up 유리 (glass material) with 거울 (mirror) — a mirror is 거울, not 유리.
Using 잔 (counter/word for glasses of drink) when you mean the glass material — those are different.

usage: Very common reason to ask about earrings/jewelry material.
재질 = material/composition; staff use it when describing products.
(으)로 만든 = made of; specifies what something is built from.
examples: 저 금속 알레르기 있어서 다른 거 없어요?
I have a metal allergy, so don't you have something else?
A genuinely useful sentence when buying earrings or watches.
이 안경테 금속이라 가볍고 튼튼해요.
These glasses frames are metal, so they're light and sturdy.
안경테 = glasses frame; 튼튼하다 = sturdy, a common product virtue.
금속 부분이 녹슬 수 있으니까 물기를 닦아 주세요.
The metal parts can rust, so please wipe off the moisture.
녹슬다 = to rust; 물기 = moisture, practical care advice.
nuance: 금속 is the general word for metal as a material, used for jewelry, frames, and hardware. The single most practical phrase is 금속 알레르기 (metal allergy), which you'll want when buying earrings, watches, or belts. For specific metals Koreans name them directly (금=gold, 은=silver, 스테인리스=stainless), but 금속 covers the category.
mistakes: Confusing 금속 (metal, the material) with 금 (gold specifically) — 금 is just one metal.
Saying 철 (iron) when you mean metal generally; 철 is specifically iron/steel.

usage: 고무+장갑 (already known); the dishwashing/cleaning gloves in every Korean home.
줄 (already known) + 고무; also the elastic in waistbands.
밑창 = sole of a shoe; non-slip rubber soles are a selling point.
재질 = material; how staff describe what something is made of.
examples: 설거지할 때 고무장갑 끼는 게 좋아요.
It's good to wear rubber gloves when washing dishes.
설거지 and 끼다 (already known); the most common use of 고무.
이 신발 밑창이 고무라서 안 미끄러워요.
This shoe's sole is rubber, so it's not slippery.
미끄럽다 (already known); non-slip is a real buying point in rainy/snowy Korea.
바지 허리가 고무줄이라 편해요.
The waist of these pants is elastic, so it's comfortable.
허리 (already known); 고무줄 waistbands are marketed as 편하다 (comfortable).
nuance: 고무 means rubber and shows up most in 고무장갑 (rubber gloves), an absolute staple of Korean kitchens you'll buy at any 마트 or 다이소. 고무줄 covers both rubber bands and the stretchy elastic in clothing waistbands. For footwear, a 고무 밑창 (rubber sole) is advertised as non-slip, which matters in Korea's rainy and icy seasons.
mistakes: Forgetting that 고무줄 means both 'rubber band' and clothing 'elastic' — context decides.
Saying 고무 신발 for rain boots; those are 장화 (already known), even though they're rubber.

usage: 그릇 (already known); the typical ceramic tableware.
컵 (already known) + 도자기 for the material.
제품 = product; a category sign at homeware shops.
전통 = traditional; sold as Korean craft souvenirs.
examples: 이 그릇 도자기예요? 전자레인지에 써도 돼요?
Is this dish ceramic? Can I use it in the microwave?
A practical check; most plain ceramic is microwave-safe but patterned ones may not be.
도자기는 떨어뜨리면 바로 깨져요.
Ceramic breaks right away if you drop it.
떨어뜨리다 and 깨지다 (already known); the fragility warning.
인사동에서 예쁜 도자기 컵을 하나 샀어요.
I bought a pretty ceramic cup in Insadong.
Insadong is the go-to spot for traditional 도자기 in Seoul.
nuance: 도자기 covers ceramics and pottery, from everyday dishes to traditional craft pieces sold in places like Insadong. It's a popular gift and souvenir category, often described as 전통 도자기. When buying for kitchen use, it's worth asking if a piece is microwave-safe, since some glazed or metallic-patterned ceramics are not.
mistakes: Confusing 도자기 (ceramic/pottery) with 유리 (glass) — they look similar when glossy but are different materials.
Microwaving 도자기 with gold/silver trim; the metallic paint can spark.

usage: 텀블러 (already known); the insulated bottle everyone carries.
냄비 (already known); a common cookware upgrade from coated pans.
Very common spoken contraction of 스테인리스; you'll hear it at markets.
식기 = tableware; the metal bowls/spoons used in many homes.
examples: 이 텀블러 스테인리스라서 보온이 잘 돼요.
This tumbler is stainless, so it keeps heat well.
보온 = heat retention; the main selling point of stainless tumblers.
스테인리스 냄비는 코팅이 안 벗겨져서 오래 써요.
Stainless pots last long because the coating doesn't peel off.
코팅 = coating, 벗겨지다 = to peel; a real durability argument.
아주머니, 이거 스뎅이에요?
Ma'am, is this stainless?
스뎅 is the natural spoken form you'd actually use at a market stall.
nuance: 스테인리스 (stainless steel) is everywhere in Korean kitchens, from 텀블러 to 냄비 to bowls. In real speech people often shorten it to 스뎅, especially at markets and homeware shops, so recognizing that slang is useful. It's marketed for durability and heat retention (보온), unlike coated pans whose coating can peel.
mistakes: Writing the full 스테인리스 스틸 every time — Korean drops 스틸 and just says 스테인리스 or 스뎅.
Assuming all shiny metal kitchenware is 스테인리스; some is aluminum (알루미늄), which is lighter.

usage: The fabric tote you use instead of plastic; very common in Korea.
(으)로 된 = made of; specifies a soft fabric material.
소파 (already known); contrasted with 가죽 (leather) sofas in stores.
부드럽다 (already known); describing texture when shopping.
examples: 이 소파 천이에요, 가죽이에요?
Is this sofa fabric or leather?
A standard either/or question when furniture shopping.
천 가방은 가벼워서 장 볼 때 좋아요.
A cloth bag is light, so it's good for grocery shopping.
장 보다 (already known) = to do grocery shopping.
천이 얇아서 비치는데 다른 색 없어요?
The fabric is thin and see-through; don't you have another color?
얇다 (already known); 비치다 = to show through, a real clothing complaint.
nuance: 천 is the general word for cloth or fabric, the soft woven material as opposed to 가죽 (leather) or 플라스틱. It's the everyday way to ask what a sofa, bag, or item is made of: 천이에요, 가죽이에요? A 천 가방 (cloth/tote bag) is especially common in Korea as an eco-friendly alternative to plastic bags.
mistakes: Confusing 천 (cloth) with the number 천 (1,000) — same sound and spelling, context decides.
Using 천 when you specifically mean cotton; cotton is 면, while 천 is fabric in general.

usage: On the tags of cheaper or sportswear clothing.
소재 = material; how the fabric type is described.
The most common specific 합성섬유 named on labels.
천연 = natural; the opposite category (cotton, wool, silk).
examples: 이 옷 합성섬유라서 잘 안 구겨져요.
This garment is synthetic, so it doesn't wrinkle easily.
구겨지다 = to get wrinkled; wrinkle resistance is a synthetic-fiber upside.
합성섬유는 땀이 잘 안 마르는 편이에요.
With synthetic fibers, sweat tends not to dry quickly.
땀 (already known); slow-drying sweat is a known downside for everyday wear.
천연섬유가 좋아요, 합성섬유가 좋아요?
Do you prefer natural fibers or synthetic ones?
Natural vs. synthetic is the basic fabric distinction when shopping.
nuance: 합성섬유 means synthetic fiber, the umbrella term for man-made fabrics like 폴리에스터 (polyester), as opposed to 천연섬유 (natural fibers) such as 면, 울, and 실크. Clothing tags use these category words, so recognizing 합성섬유 100% tells you a garment is fully man-made. Synthetics resist wrinkles but can feel less breathable, which matters in humid Korean summers.
mistakes: Mixing up 합성섬유 (synthetic) with 천연섬유 (natural) — they're opposites on the care label.
Thinking 합성섬유 is always bad; sportswear is intentionally synthetic for stretch and quick movement.
